Each represents a distinct violated atomic obligation. The synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf is a compiler artifact supporting the initial-entry defect rather than a separate deadlock issue, per the compiler-owned placeholder boundary rule.

arguments.reason: The behavior_consequence lens identifies three independent frontier failures caused by the initial entry defect: (1) the root initial edge targets a compiler-synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state instead of the NL-required DoorShut, (2) all six real operating states are unreachable from root, and (3) all eight events have declared consumers but zero reachable consumers. Beyond these frontier properties, the lens also identifies one missing transition (DoorOpen→DoorShut on Door Closed), one missing guard (cooking-time-is-zero on DoorOpenWithItem→DoorShutWithItem), two missing state actions (ReadytoCook display/update, Cooking timer start), and two missing transition effects (Cancel cooking-time update, Door-Opened timer stop). Each represents a distinct violated atomic obligation. The synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf is a compiler artifact supporting the initial-entry defect rather than a separate deadlock issue, per the compiler-owned placeholder boundary rule.

issues.requirement_quote: The microwave starts in the DoorShut state. From this state, the system can either remain in DoorShut if a Cancel action is performed or transition to the DoorOpen state when the door is opened.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The consumer transitions are correctly wired among the 6 real states and cover all 8 events. If the initial entry defect were corrected, all 15 consumer transitions would become reachable and operational coverage would be complete. The coverage failure is entirely a causal consequence of the synthetic initial target.
issues.title: All eight events have zero reachable consumers in root scope

issues.basis: NL5: 'entering cooking time takes the system to ReadytoCook, where the cooking time is displayed and updated.' FCSTM state:ReadytoCook:line:15 exists. Reference inspection: actions count=0, abstract_action_inventory=[]. No S4 phase hint available from NL.
issues.expected: The ReadytoCook state must carry an action that displays and updates the cooking time, representing the state's ongoing behavioral obligation.
issues.observed: The FCSTM has no actions defined anywhere: reference_inspection_facts shows actions count=0 and abstract_action_inventory is empty. The ReadytoCook state (line 15) exists as a carrier but has no action content.
issues.reason: NL5 states that in the ReadytoCook state, 'the cooking time is displayed and updated.' This is a state_action obligation. The NL does not specify a lifecycle phase (entry/do/exit), so S4 is not applicable. The precise claim remains a predicate-null candidate for W1 adjudication.
issues.requirement_quote: where the cooking time is displayed and updated
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML source is a simple state diagram without do/entry/exit action notation, so the FCSTM faithfully reflects the source's lack of action syntax. However, the NL explicitly requires this behavioral content, making it a genuine specification-to-model gap regardless of the source notation's limitations.
issues.title: Missing cooking time display and update action in ReadytoCook state

issues.basis: NL6: 'if the Cancel action is performed, the system returns to DoorShutWithItem, canceling or updating the cooking time.' FCSTM transition:line:27 effects=[]. Reference inspection: effects count implied by empty lists on all 16 transitions.
issues.expected: The Cancel transition from ReadytoCook to DoorShutWithItem must have the effect of canceling or updating the cooking time variable.
issues.observed: The FCSTM transition:line:27 (ReadytoCook -> DoorShutWithItem : /Cancel) has an empty effects list. No transition in the entire model carries any effect. The model also has zero variables declared.
issues.reason: NL6 explicitly states that the Cancel action from ReadytoCook returns to DoorShutWithItem 'canceling or updating the cooking time.' This is an effect obligation on the specific transition. The FCSTM transition exists but carries no effect. No frozen predicate covers transition effects, so this remains predicate-null W1.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The transition endpoint is correct and the trigger is correct. The missing effect is a behavioral side-effect annotation that the simple PlantUML notation does not express. The structural connectivity obligation is satisfied; only the effect annotation is absent.

issues.basis: NL7: 'the system transitions to the Cooking state, where the timer starts.' FCSTM state:Cooking:line:16 exists. Reference inspection: actions count=0. No explicit phase word in NL.
issues.expected: The Cooking state must carry an action that starts the timer, representing the state's entry behavioral obligation.
issues.observed: The FCSTM has no actions defined anywhere. The Cooking state (line 16) exists as a carrier but has no action content. The model also has zero variables, so no timer variable is declared.
issues.reason: NL7 states that the system transitions to Cooking 'where the timer starts.' This is a state_action obligation on the Cooking state. The NL does not explicitly name a lifecycle phase (entry/do/exit), so S4 is not applicable. The precise claim remains a predicate-null candidate.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML source does not use action notation on states. The NL says 'where the timer starts' which could be interpreted as an entry action, but the NL does not explicitly use the word 'entry' or 'on entry.' The phase is ambiguous between entry and do, preventing S4 application.
issues.title: Missing timer start action in Cooking state

issues.basis: NL8: 'opening the door stops the timer and the system transitions to DoorOpenWithItem.' FCSTM transition:line:30 effects=[]. Reference inspection: no effects on any transition.
